back: The lifelong process of learning the norms, values, language, skills and roles of society so that a person can live and work with others.
A person, group or institution that teaches an individual how to behave in society: family, school, peers, community, religious groups, media.
Learning in early childhood, mainly within the family: language, personal care, manners and family values.
Later, lifelong learning outside the home through the school, peers, religion, community, workplace and media.

Name five methods the family uses to socialise children.
back: Instruction, example (role modelling), rewards and sanctions, stories/songs/proverbs, and participation in work.

front: Why is the family the most important agent in early childhood?
back: It comes first, the child spends most time there and depends on its members completely, so early lessons last for life.

front: Norm or value: 'children greet elders first'?
back: A norm (a rule of behaviour). The value behind it is respect for elders.
